name: Flipt
description: Protects against destructive Flipt CLI and API operations.

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-flag-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt flag delete permanently removes a feature flag. This cannot be undone.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Flipt feature flag immediately removes it from evaluation. All \ applications checking this flag will receive default values or errors. Rules, \ variants, and distributions associated with the flag are also removed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - flipt flag get: Review flag configuration first \ - Disable the flag instead of deleting \ - Export flag configuration before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-segment-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt segment delete removes a segment and its constraints.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a segment removes user grouping rules. Any flags using this segment \ for targeting will lose that targeting logic, potentially changing which users \ receive which variants.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - flipt segment get: Review segment configuration \ - Check which flags reference this segment \ - Update flags to use different segments first

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-namespace-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt namespace delete removes a namespace and all its flags, segments, and rules.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a namespace removes ALL flags, segments, rules, and constraints \ within it. This is a complete wipe of that feature flag environment. All \ applications using this namespace will lose flag evaluations.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - flipt namespace get: Review namespace contents \ - Export all flags and segments before deletion \ - Migrate resources to another namespace first

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-rule-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt rule delete removes a targeting rule from a flag.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a rule changes how the flag evaluates for targeted users. Users \ previously matching this rule will fall through to other rules or receive \ the default variant.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - flipt rule get: Review rule configuration \ - Disable the rule instead of deleting \ - Verify other rules handle affected users

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-constraint-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt constraint delete removes a constraint from a segment.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a constraint changes segment membership. Users previously excluded \ or included by this constraint will now match or not match the segment \ differently.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review segment membership before and after \ - Test constraint changes in a staging namespace \ - Document why the constraint is being removed

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-variant-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt variant delete removes a variant from a flag.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a variant removes a possible flag value. Rules distributing traffic \ to this variant will fail or need adjustment. Applications expecting this \ variant value may break.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Check which rules reference this variant \ - Update distributions before deleting \ - Zero out traffic to this variant first

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-distribution-delete
destructive_patterns.description: flipt distribution delete removes a distribution from a rule.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a distribution changes traffic allocation within a rule. The \ affected variant will no longer receive traffic from this rule, shifting \ all traffic to remaining distributions.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review current traffic allocation \ - Adjust percentages instead of deleting \ - Verify other distributions handle the traffic

destructive_patterns.name: flipt-api-delete
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE request to Flipt API can remove flags, segments, or rules.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API DELETE calls to Flipt can remove flags, segments, rules, or \ namespaces without CLI confirmation prompts. API deletions take effect \ immediately across all connected applications.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use the Flipt CLI for better confirmation prompts \ - GET the resource first to verify what will be deleted \ - Use the Flipt UI for visibility into dependencies
